newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch PTT will not increase bid for TNT.
newsitem.headline: Dutch PTT will not increase bid for TNT.

text.p: Dutch post and telecoms group PTT Nederland NV said on Monday it would not increase its bid for TNT.

"KPN declares that its recommended cash offers of AUD 2.45 per share for each of the ordinary and converting preference shares of TNT, in the absence of a bid from a third party, will not be increased," the company said in a statement.

KPN is currently entitled, as a result of market purchases and acceptances received, to 20.5 percent of the issued ordinary shares of TNT and 20.4 percent of the issued convertible preference shares of TNT.
KPN's ordinary and convertible preference offers are being extended and will remain open for acceptance until 3rd December, 1996.
Last week the European Commission approved KPN's recommended cash offer for TNT.

On 31th October, the Australian Treasurer decided to raise no objections to KPN's proposed acquisition of TNT and the US anti-trust Hert-Scott-Rodino waiting period in respect of KPN's offer has been terminated.
"Accordingly, all of the regulatory conditions to KPN's offer for TNT ordinary and TNT convertible preference shares have now been satisfied," it said.
